title: We've been trying for five months to register as a certified auditor under the Serbian Information Security Law so we can bid on public procurement contracts, but the paperwork at the Ministry keeps bouncing back for minor formal reasons and we don't know how to fix it.

record.text: We've been trying for five months to register as a certified auditor under the Serbian Information Security Law so we can bid on public procurement contracts, but the paperwork at the Ministry keeps bouncing back for minor formal reasons and we don't know how to fix it.
record.detail: Serbian law on information security requires that organisations in certain sectors use certified auditors for their mandatory audits. That certification would open public procurement to us, which currently we cannot bid on at all. We applied to the Ministry five months ago and have had the application returned three times, each time with a short note citing a formal deficiency. The first return was about the formatting of an attached document. The second was about a reference number on a supporting form. The third cited an unclear clause about professional experience documentation. We have tried reading the relevant rulebook ourselves and consulting a general business lawyer in Subotica who was honest enough to say she does not know this specific regulatory area well. We are not looking for legal advice in the strict sense — we just need someone who has successfully navigated this specific process and can look at our application package and tell us concretely what is wrong. A good outcome is a submitted application that does not come back. We would like to resolve this within the next three months because there is a municipal procurement round opening in the autumn that we want to be eligible for.
